lesson.title: May I Help You? The Art of Professional Service
lesson.content:
Welcome to Grade 11 English! We start with the most essential skill for any vocational professional: **Making Offers and Suggestions**. In the workplace, being proactive is key. You will learn how to offer help using phrases like 'May I assist you with...?', 'Would you like me to...?', and 'Can I give you a hand?'.

For SMK students, this is the foundation of **Customer Service**. Whether you are in a hotel, a workshop, or an IT helpdesk, how you offer help defines your professionalism. We also learn how to accept or decline offers politely. Remember, English is not just about words; it's about the attitude of being helpful and professional in a global environment. Let's practice being a proactive problem solver!

subject: Bahasa Inggris
subtopic: Giving Suggestions in a Professional Context

lesson.title: I Suggest That...: Contributing Ideas to the Team
lesson.content:
A good technician doesn't just follow orders; they provide solutions. We will learn how to give suggestions using 'I suggest that...', 'Why don't we...?', or 'How about...?'. Giving suggestions shows that you are thinking critically about your work and the company's efficiency.

You will practice giving suggestions for workplace improvements, such as saving energy or organizing tools better. Learning to express your ideas politely but clearly in English will make you a valuable team member in any international company. Don't be afraid to speak up; your ideas matter! Let's build your confidence in sharing professional insights.

lesson.title: In My Opinion: Joining the Professional Debate
lesson.content:
In a meeting, you need to share your thoughts. We will learn how to state opinions using 'In my opinion...', 'I personally believe...', and 'From my point of view...'. We also cover how to agree or disagree politely using 'I totally agree with you' or 'I see your point, but I have a different perspective'.

Constructive debate is common in the industry. For example, which software is better for this project? Which material is more cost-effective? By mastering these expressions, you can participate in professional discussions effectively. English helps you negotiate and collaborate with people from different backgrounds. Let's learn how to defend your ideas with logic and respect.

subject: Bahasa Inggris
subtopic: Writing and Responding to Formal Invitations

lesson.title: You Are Cordially Invited: Business Event Etiquette
lesson.content:
Formal events are part of the professional world. You will learn how to write **Formal Invitations** for grand openings, seminars, or company anniversaries. We will study the structure: Host, Event, Date, Venue, and R.S.V.P. We also learn how to respond to these invitations formally.

For SMK students, knowing how to handle formal invitations shows that you understand **Business Etiquette**. Whether you are inviting a client to a product launch or responding to a job interview invitation, your tone must be polite and professional. English is your passport to high-level networking and professional growth. Let's practice the language of formal social interaction!

lesson.title: Why It Matters: Building Persuasive Arguments
lesson.content:
**Analytical Exposition** is a text that persuades the reader that something is an important matter. You will learn the structure: Thesis (your position), Arguments (supporting facts), and Reiteration (restating your position). For SMK students, this is useful for writing proposals or pitching ideas.

For example, you might write an exposition on 'Why Digital Literacy is Crucial for Modern Workers' or 'The Importance of Green Technology in Manufacturing'. You learn to use connecting words like 'Firstly', 'Moreover', and 'Therefore'. Mastering this will make you a persuasive communicator who can influence others with data and logic in the global market.

subject: Bahasa Inggris
subtopic: Using Passive Voice in Technical Reports

lesson.title: Focused on the Action: Mastering Passive Voice
lesson.content:
In technical writing and manuals, we often care more about 'what happened' than 'who did it'. This is why we use **Passive Voice** (e.g., 'The machine is serviced once a month' instead of 'The technician services the machine'). You will learn the formula: *To Be + Past Participle (V3)*.

Passive voice makes your reports sound objective and professional. For example, 'The software was updated' or 'The data is being processed'. It is the standard language of science and industry. By using passive voice correctly, your technical descriptions will be clearer and more formal, making you sound like a true expert in your field.

subject: Bahasa Inggris
subtopic: Writing Professional Personal Letters and Emails

lesson.title: Dear Colleague: Effective Email Communication
lesson.content:
In the digital age, emails are the most common way to communicate. We will learn how to write professional personal letters/emails to colleagues or mentors. We study the informal yet professional tone, including salutations, the body, and closing. You'll learn the difference between 'Best regards' and 'Sincerely yours'.

For SMK students, being able to write a clear and polite email is a 'must-have' skill. Whether you are asking for advice from a senior or coordinating a small task with a teammate, your writing reflects your character. We will practice writing emails for asking permissions, giving updates, and saying thank you. Let's make sure your digital communication is top-notch!

lesson.title: Step by Step: Reading Manuals Like a Pro
lesson.content:
Most high-tech equipment comes with manuals in English. We will study **Procedure Texts** specifically for technical guides. You will learn to recognize imperatives (commands like 'Switch on', 'Connect', 'Rotate') and sequence adverbs. We also focus on understanding 'Warnings' and 'Cautions' to ensure safety.

Being able to follow a manual correctly in English means you can handle international-standard tools and software. We will practice reading manuals for gadgets, software installation, or machine maintenance. This skill makes you an independent learner who can troubleshoot problems without waiting for others. Let's sharpen your technical reading skills for a successful career!

subject: Bahasa Inggris
subtopic: Explaining How Things Work in Industry

lesson.title: How It Works: Explaining Technical Processes
lesson.content:
**Explanation Text** explains how or why something occurs. Structure: General Statement and Sequenced Explanation. For SMK students, this is used to explain processes like 'How a solar panel generates electricity' or 'How an engine cools down'. We use technical terms and causal conjunctions.

You will learn how to explain your vocational processes to non-experts or clients in English. This is a high-level skill that proves you truly understand your field. Being able to explain the 'logic' behind a machine or a system in English will set you apart from basic workers and put you on the path to becoming a manager or a specialist.

lesson.title: Inquiry: Asking for Information and Prices
lesson.content:
In business, we often need to ask for information or prices (Inquiry). You will learn how to write an **Inquiry Letter** politely and clearly. Phrases like 'I am writing to inquire about...', 'Could you please send us your latest catalog?', and 'We would appreciate it if...' are essential. We also learn how to write a professional reply to such inquiries.

For SMK students, especially in business and marketing, this is a daily task. Even for technical majors, you might need to ask for spare part availability from an overseas supplier. Learning to handle business inquiries in English will help you build networks and trust with international partners. Let's get down to business with professional writing!

lesson.title: The Perfect Candidate: Interview Skills (Part 1)
lesson.content:
Getting a job in a multinational company requires a great interview in English. We will practice answering common questions like 'Tell me about yourself', 'What are your strengths?', and 'Why should we hire you?'. You will learn to use positive adjectives to describe your vocational skills and work ethics.

We focus on the STAR method (Situation, Task, Action, Result) to tell stories about your achievements during school projects or internships. This lesson builds your confidence to present yourself as a competent and motivated professional. Remember, an interview is not an exam; it's a conversation where you show your value. Let's get you ready for your dream job!

lesson.title: Hello, This is...: Professional Phone Etiquette
lesson.content:
Talking on the phone in English can be scary because you can't see the other person. We will learn common phrases for making a call, taking a message, and transferring a call. Phrases like 'Who's calling, please?', 'Could you hold the line?', and 'I'll put you through' are the standard.

For SMK students, handling phone calls professionally is a vital part of communication skills. You will practice how to spell names using the phonetic alphabet and how to clarify information if you didn't hear it clearly. Being calm and polite on the phone will give a great impression of you and your company. Let's master the art of professional telephoning!

lesson.title: Show and Tell: Presenting Your Project
lesson.content:
In the workplace, you often need to present your project or findings. You will learn how to structure a presentation: Introduction (Greeting, Hook, Outline), Body (Main points), and Conclusion (Summary, Q&A). We focus on 'Signposting'—words that guide the audience through your talk (e.g., 'Moving on to...', 'In conclusion...').

You will practice presenting a simple technical topic from your major. Using visuals and clear English, you will learn how to engage an audience and answer their questions confidently. Presentation skills are 'leadership' skills. By mastering this, you are preparing to lead teams and represent your company at the highest levels. Let's shine on the professional stage!

lesson.title: Danger! English for Workplace Safety
lesson.content:
Safety is non-negotiable. Many safety signs and PPE instructions are in English. We will learn vocabulary related to hazards (flammable, toxic, corrosive) and safety gear (goggles, ear protection, harness). We also practice following emergency procedures in English.

For SMK students, understanding safety English could save lives. You will learn how to report an accident and how to explain safety rules to others. Being 'safety-conscious' in a global language shows that you are a mature and responsible worker. Let's ensure you can work safely anywhere in the world by mastering the universal language of safety!

lesson.title: Global Ready: Final Reflection and Portfolio
lesson.content:
Congratulations! You have completed the Grade 11 English curriculum. You can now offer help, share opinions, write formal invitations, and explain technical processes in English. The most important lesson is: **English is a tool to open doors to the world**.

Keep practicing your speaking and writing every day. Use English to learn new things from international websites and videos. You are now more ready than ever to compete in the global job market. Don't stop here; make English a part of your professional identity. Your future is bright, and the world is waiting for your skills. Good luck, global professional! Merdeka!

lesson.title: Making a Deal: Negotiating with Offers
lesson.content: In business, offers are often negotiated. We will learn how to bargain or counter-offer politely using phrases like 'That's a bit high, can you do...?', 'What if we offer you a discount?', or 'If you buy two, we will...'. This is essential for students in marketing and sales. However, even for technical majors, you might need to negotiate for budget or resources for your project. Negotiation is about finding a win-win solution where both parties are happy.

lesson.title: Professional Advice: Seeking and Giving Guidance
lesson.content: Asking for advice shows humility and a willingness to learn. Giving advice shows expertise. We will learn phrases like 'What do you think I should do?', 'I would recommend...', or 'If I were you, I would...'. In the workplace, giving advice to a junior or asking for it from a senior is a common way to grow. We focus on being helpful and constructive without being pushy. Professional advice should always be based on facts and experience.

lesson.title: Global Etiquette: Invitations in Different Cultures
lesson.content: An invitation in Japan might be different from an invitation in the USA. We will study the cultural nuances and expectations in formal invitations across the globe. You will learn about appropriate attire (dress codes), punctuality, and gift-giving traditions. Understanding these differences shows that you are a culturally intelligent (CQ) professional. Being respectful of other people's customs through English will help you build stronger and more lasting international business relationships.

lesson.title: Pitching Excellence: The Business Proposal
lesson.content: A business proposal is basically an analytical exposition with a goal to get a project approved. We will learn how to write the 'Need' (Problem), 'Solution' (Your Idea), and 'Benefits' (Why it works). We use strong adjectives and persuasive verbs. For SMK students, this is the key to winning competitions or getting funding for your startup. A well-written proposal in English shows that you are not just a worker, but a visionary who can create value for others.

subject: Bahasa Inggris
subtopic: Passive Voice in Quality Control Logs

lesson.title: Logged and Checked: Passive Voice for QC
lesson.content: Quality Control (QC) logs are almost always written in the passive voice. 'The component was inspected', 'The temperature was recorded', 'The error was corrected'. This style emphasizes the standard procedure over the individual worker. We will practice writing log entries for various industrial scenarios. This helps you maintain a high level of accuracy and objectivity in your professional documentation, ensuring that your records meet international auditing standards.

subject: Bahasa Inggris
subtopic: Writing a Thank-You Letter after an Interview

lesson.title: The Follow-Up: The Power of the Thank-You Letter
lesson.content: Sending a thank-you email after an interview can make you stand out. We will learn how to write a short, professional message that expresses gratitude and reiterates your interest in the position. Phrases like 'Thank you for your time today...', 'I particularly enjoyed learning about...', and 'I look forward to hearing from you' are vital. This small gesture shows your enthusiasm and professionalism, often giving you an edge over other candidates who didn't follow up.

lesson.title: Fixing Problems: Troubleshooting in English
lesson.content: Troubleshooting is a special kind of procedure. It usually follows an 'If... then...' logic. 'If the light is red, then check the battery'. We will learn how to read and write these guides. You will practice identifying symptoms and prescribing solutions using technical English. This skill is critical for IT, mechanical, and electrical majors. Being able to solve technical problems using English-language resources will make you an expert who can handle any challenge in a global workplace.

lesson.title: The Big Picture: Describing the Supply Chain
lesson.content: No product is made in isolation. We will use explanation texts to describe how materials move from suppliers to the factory and then to customers (Supply Chain). You will learn terms like 'Raw materials', 'Logistics', 'Wholesaler', and 'Retailer'. Explaining the flow of goods and information in English shows that you understand the global economy. This bird's-eye view is essential for anyone aspiring to be a manager or a logistics specialist in an international corporation.

lesson.title: Order Placed: Purchasing English
lesson.content: After an inquiry, you might place an order. We will learn the vocabulary of purchasing: 'Quantity', 'Unit Price', 'Delivery Date', and 'Payment Terms'. You will learn how to write an Order Letter and how to send an Order Confirmation. We also cover how to report a wrong order or a delay politely but firmly. Clear communication in purchasing prevents costly mistakes and ensures that your vocational projects have all the materials they need on time.

subject: Bahasa Inggris
subtopic: Asking Intelligent Questions to the Employer

lesson.title: Your Turn to Ask: Interview Skills (Part 2)
lesson.content: At the end of an interview, they always ask, 'Do you have any questions for us?'. Saying 'No' is a mistake. We will learn how to ask intelligent questions about the company culture, the team, and future growth. Questions like 'What does a typical day look like here?' or 'What are the opportunities for training?' show that you are serious and ambitious. This is your chance to show that you are looking for a career, not just a job. Let's make you the most memorable candidate!

lesson.title: Leave a Message: Voicemail Etiquette
lesson.content: If someone doesn't answer, you need to leave a voicemail. We will learn how to be concise and clear: State your name, your company, the reason for the call, and your phone number. We also learn how to record a professional voicemail greeting for your own phone. Phrases like 'I'm calling regarding...', 'Please get back to me at...', and 'I look forward to your call' are the standard. This skill ensures that your communication doesn't stop even when you can't talk live.

lesson.title: Answering Tough Questions: The Q&A Session
lesson.content: The most difficult part of a presentation is the Q&A. We will learn phrases for clarifying questions ('Could you repeat that?'), stalling for time ('That's an interesting question...'), and admitting if you don't know the answer yet ('I'll check and get back to you'). We focus on being honest and helpful. Answering questions well proves that you are an expert who knows your subject deeply. It builds trust with your audience and shows your ability to think on your feet in English.

lesson.title: Incident Report: Reporting Hazards in English
lesson.content: Preventing accidents is everyone's job. We will learn how to write a 'Near-Miss' or 'Hazard Report' in English. You will practice describing what happened, where it happened, and what the potential danger was. Using clear and objective English helps the safety team take action immediately. By being a 'Safety Champion' who can report issues in a global language, you contribute to a better and safer work environment for everyone in your international company.

lesson.title: Staying Updated: Researching Industry Trends
lesson.content: The best professionals always know the latest trends. We will learn how to use English-language search engines and news sites to research trends in your specific major (e.g., AI in IT, Electric Vehicles in Automotive). You will practice summarizing an article and sharing the main points with your class. This habit of 'Global Research' ensures that your skills never become obsolete and that you are always ready for the next big innovation in your career.

subject: Bahasa Inggris
subtopic: Preparing for the Final Project and Career

lesson.title: The Road Ahead: English for Your Career Path
lesson.content: As you move toward Grade 12, English will become even more important for your final project and job search. We reflect on your progress and set goals for the future. You are now a competent communicator who can navigate professional situations in English. Remember to keep your English portfolio updated with your best work. The skills you've learned here are not just for school; they are for your life. Keep dreaming big, keep working hard, and keep using English to reach your goals. The world is yours! Merdeka!
